name: The Racial Equity Institute
selfDescription: A Black-owned business comprised of a multiracial team of organizers and trainers devoted to anti-racism transformation and structural-racism education.
mission: REI maintains a movement orientation, always focused on institutional change with equitable and just outcomes for everyone.
philosophy: Racism operates at institutional and systemic levels independent of individual intention. REI's analysis addresses social systems themselves, not individual deficits. Power is at the root of human experience.
groundwaterMetaphor: If you find dead fish in one lake, you ask what's wrong with the fish. If you find dead fish in every lake in the region, you analyze the groundwater. Racial disparities show up in every system — education, health, housing, justice — so the cause is structural, in the groundwater, not in the fish.
history: Founded in 2012 by Deena Hayes-Greene (Managing Director) and Suzanne Plihcik, both former lead trainers for Dismantling Racism Works (DRWorks/Changework) and the People's Institute for Survival and Beyond. After DRWorks director Kenneth Jones died, Plihcik (with Bree Carlson) completed his contracts; Hayes then joined Plihcik, and REI was incorporated under Hayes's leadership and creative vision. REI neither advertised nor sought work through proposals — it went nowhere uninvited, and the number of requests doubled in short order. Today REI's trainer corps includes more than 40 multiracial, multi-generational trainers from education, healthcare, law enforcement, nonprofits, and business.

policies: Booking requests are confirmed or declined within 10 business days.
Cancellation fewer than 15 days out incurs a 50% charge; 45+ days out, no penalty.
REI does not issue certificates; hosts may provide them.
Workbooks are included with most workshops.
Virtual workshops: one participant per registration — screens may not be shared.
